post.caption: Rhodonite is Russia's pink eagle stone. Old Ural tales say eagles carried the stones to their nests. The name rhodonite comes from the Greek word for rose. Manganese gives it a pink to rose red color. Black manganese oxides thread through the pink as spidery veins. Where rhodonite is exposed, the surface can darken to brown or black. Ural rhodonite was first found and worked in the late 1700s. Ural workshops carved vases and other objects from it. Columns in one Moscow metro station are faced with pink rhodonite. Massachusetts named rhodonite its official state gem.
